decisions.reason: ACE3 was launched publicly as a new industry standard for ALCMS, sits at the core of the firm's airfield lighting business and carries heavy investment, so dropping it would write off that investment and contradict the firm's announced direction.
The air situation display builds on the firm's tower and surveillance offer, was moved onto a page of its own, and fits the integrated operations strategy, so management would persist with it.
The training program costs little to keep and supports the service portfolio, and any weak uptake can be blamed on the temporary pandemic slump in air travel.

This airfield lighting course was only mentioned on the website and carries little commitment, which makes it the easiest to drop, but it is cheap to run and supports the core lighting business, so it stays.
The collaboration software is central to the publicly announced vision of collaborative decision-making and integrated operations, so management is strongly committed to it.
The MLAT system was announced with fanfare at inter airport Europe and required substantial R&D, so disappointing results would likely be attributed to the temporary COVID downturn in aviation.
